claims.text: The starting material is HfZrTiTa0.53 with quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 exhibits limited strain hardening and early failure under high-strain-rate adiabatic loading.
Controlled cold rolling followed by annealing can induce a fine three-dimensional deformation-twin network in HfZrTiTa0.53.
A three-dimensional twin network can block dislocations impinging on twin boundaries.
Intersecting twin–matrix interfaces can provide pathways for dislocation glide and cross-slip.
Twin-boundary migration provides additional strain hardening.
Deformation twinning can increase strain-hardening rates in suitable alloys.
The twin architecture promotes more uniformly distributed plastic deformation.
The induced twin network will delay localized shear-band formation and the associated rapid failure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will have a higher dynamic strain-hardening rate than the as-cast baseline.
Processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will sustain prolonged uniform deformation and greater effective dynamic ductility.
Processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will have greater resistance to deformation localization.
The intervention will moderate impact-induced energy release and improve energy absorption during high-rate loading.
The predicted benefits apply primarily under adiabatic dynamic loading near 10^3 s^-1 at ambient or moderately elevated temperature.
CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy provides precedent for a three-dimensional twin architecture that combines twin-boundary strengthening with dislocation glide and cross-slip pathways.
